The '''bordoks''' were a vaguely [[Equine/Legends|equine]] [[Diet/Legends|herbivore]] native to the forest [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. They were used by [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] as pack animals and mounts when tamed. Bordoks were very sure-footed and, in spite of their size, capable of carrying very large loads.

{{Creature-stub}}

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Bordok-aa.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Lesser bordoks]]
Forest dwelling<ref name="WSW">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> Bordoks were medium-sized, [[Horse/Legends|pony]]-like animals best known as [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] employed them as beasts of burden,<ref name="A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> although similar creatures existed on many planets throughout the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref> Bordoks had long manes, gentle features, and strong backs.<ref name="EGAS" />

Although somewhat similar in appearance to [[Horse/Legends|horses]], bordoks were not true equines. They had upward-curving horns that were short on young [[Gender/Legends|females]] but could grow larger on an adult male.<ref name="AA" /> Bordoks also had split hooves that helped them climb through the [[Tree/Legends|trees]] of their arboreal home.

There were two [[Species/Legends|species]] of bordoks: The lesser bordok grew to no more than 1.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall at the shoulder. The rarer greater bordok could reach twice this size. Both species were fairly intelligent, and were not startled easily. However, they did instinctively become more skittish at night due to the various nocturnal predators that stalked the moon's surface.<ref name="AA" />

Some have been known to show a remarkable amount of intelligenge, enough to cause [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] to begin readdressing the level of their [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]].<ref name="EGAS" />

==Domestication==
Borsoks made strong ties to their owners and were often considerated part of the family.<ref name="EGAS" /> Adult bordoks were extremely protective of their young and, when domesticated, over their master as well.<ref name="AA" /> Herding instinct was so strong that adult males sometimes sacrificed themselves for the good of the herd, fighting predators while the others escaped. Young bordoks were commonly taken as pets and often developed lifelong bonds with their owners. [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]] had a pet baby lesser bordok named [[Baga]].

[[Bordok bath toy]]s<ref name="SW-Let's Go Play Ball: Toys and Games from a Galaxy Far, Far Away">{{SW|url=news/lets-go-play-ball-toys-and-games-from-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Let's Go Play Ball: Toys and Games from a Galaxy Far, Far Away|nolive=1}}</ref> were available in the galaxy.<ref name="The Pirates of Tarnoonga">{{DroidsCite|The Pirates of Tarnoonga}}</ref>

"[[Bordok feathers]]" was an [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] phrase that was used to express contempt for a foolish thought or idea.<ref name="The Haunted Village">{{Ewoks|The Haunted Village}}</ref>

The Ewoks of the [[Gondula]] tribe kept a herd of bordoks in a pen in their [[Southern Ewok Lake Village]].<ref name="SWG:ELV">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=poi|Ewok Lake Village|Endor}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Bordoks made their first appearance in ''[[Wicket Finds a Way: An Ewok Adventure]]'', a [[1984]] children's book written by [[Melinda Luke]] and published by [[Random House]].<ref name="Wicket Finds a Way: An Ewok Adventure">''[[Wicket Finds a Way: An Ewok Adventure]]''</ref> Their first appearance as toys was in the brief toy line [[Wicket the Ewok (toy line)|''Wicket the Ewok'']] made as part of [[Kenner Products|Kenner Prescholar]].<ref>{{KennerCite|set=Wicket the Ewok (toy line)|pack=Ewok Family Hut|altlink=http://blog.theswca.com/2017/10/woktots-kenners-preschool-star-wars-toys.html}}</ref>
